newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: RISE IN RETAIL TRADE ENCOURAGING
Acting Federal Treasurer, Jim Short, says the rise in retail trade in August is encouraging and supports Budget forecasts of solid economic growth this financial year.
Retail trade grew by one-point-one per cent in the month, following a one per cent rise in July.
Senator Short has rejected Opposition claims economic activity is subdued, saying the figures show the deficit can be cut while solid growth is achieved in the short term.
The Acting Treasurer says the Budget strategy is the basis for stronger, sustained growth over the medium term, but has warned the Senate has to pass the Budget in order to achieve higher growth.
HOWARD SAYS GOVT ATTITUDE TO ASIA IS WHAT COUNTS
Prime Minister John Howard says what matters in Asia is the attitude of the Australian Government.
That follows a warning from Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer, that Independent Pauline Hanson's comments could impact on Australia's trade with Asia.
Mr Fischer has warned Ms Hanson's comments, which have been reported in the Asian media, could harm trade, investment and jobs.
But Mr Howard has declined to back Mr Fisher's warning.
ACTU SAYS EMPLOYERS TRYING TO DRAG OUT CASE
ACTU President Jennie George has accused employer groups of trying to drag out the ACTU's Living Wage Case.
The case has resumed this morning in the Industrial Relations Commission in Melbourne.
The ACTU is arguing that the case should proceed without delay despite claims from employers that it should not go ahead, until the Government's Workplace Relations Bill is passed.
Ms George says the Commission should as always, deal with the law as it stands.
HOWARD DEFENDS AWARDING OF AD CONTRACT
Prime Minister, John Howard, has defended the awarding of a contract to advertise the gun buy-back scheme to DDB Needham.

Labor Senator, Robert Ray, claimed there was a conflict of interest because DDB Needham avertises for the Liberal party, and three people on the committee which awarded the contract are former Liberal party officials.
On Perth radio station, 6PR, Mr Howard decribed claims of a conflict of interest as nonsense, and said nothing unethical's been done.
GOLD FALL A BLIP IN MARKET, SAYS BROKER
A leading stockbroker says the price fall of gold is a blip in the longterm market and should correct itself within six months.
The price has fallen below 300-and-80 dollars U.S an ounce for the first time in 12 months.
Stock-broker, David Reid, says gold is following other metals in the downward trend that's been exacerbated by the International Monetary Fund's plans to sell up to five-million ounces.
However, Mr Reid says if this sell-off is done in an orderly fashion over five years, as happened in the 1970s, it might not hurt the precious metal.
ACT'S WORST ACCIDENT SINCE 1989
Police are examining whether a Mitsubishi van which burst into flames in Canberra killing four people was defective.
A 40-year-old man his three daughters aged six, seven and eleven died on the Monaro Highway at Symonston last night in the ACT's worst road accident since 1989.
The victims were from Canberra but their names have not been released.
Police spokesman, Steve Thorn says the car did a 360 degree turn before hitting a street light and bursting into flames.
Constable Thorn says the cause of the fire is still to be determined.
SUPERLEAGUE DECISION DUE ON FRIDAY
Three Federal judges are due to hand down their decision on the Superleague appeal this Friday.
News Limited has challenged a ruling stopping its breakaway competition from kicking off until the year 2000.
A Federal court spokesman says the Full Bench will publish its judgement in Sydney on Friday afternoon.
